score_rationale: Clear buyer population (pharma reps, behavioral health SaaS, addiction treatment staffing agencies) with documented willingness to pay in adjacent markets. SAMHSA publishes N-SSATS public use data as a direct download. Dataset is facility-level (no PII — all records are organizations/clinics, not individuals). Score 7 not 8 because the behavioral health vertical is slightly more niche than the mass-market OSHA or SBA datasets; however, pharmaceutical rep buyers are among the most willing-to-pay B2B audiences in existence.
summary: A cleaned CSV of 15,000+ US substance abuse and mental health treatment facilities sourced from the SAMHSA National Survey of Substance Abuse Treatment Services (N-SSATS) public use dataset — an annual survey published by SAMHSA as a downloadable data file without authentication. Each facility record includes the facility name, street address, city, state, ZIP, facility type (residential, outpatient, hospital, methadone clinic, detox), ownership (private for-profit, private non-profit, state/county), services offered (medication-assisted treatment, detox, dual-diagnosis, adolescent programs, LGBTQ+-specific), payment accepted (Medicaid, Medicare, private insurance, sliding scale), and whether the facility is SAMHSA-certified. This dataset is distinct from the NPPES mental health directory already in the catalog — that file covers individual practitioners by NPI code; this covers treatment facilities as organizations. CenterSite, Behavioral Health Business, and treatment center marketing agencies charge $500–$5,000/month for facility-level directory access and targeted lists. A one-time $49 CSV targets pharmaceutical representatives, behavioral health SaaS vendors, addiction treatment staffing agencies, and recovery services providers — none of whom need a $5,000/month platform to run a single outreach campaign.

audience.who: Pharmaceutical sales representatives and regional managers from addiction medicine companies (Indivior, BraeBurn, Alkermes) who promote buprenorphine/naltrexone/naloxone products and need a facility-level list of every MAT (medication-assisted treatment) clinic, methadone clinic, and inpatient detox program in their territory; behavioral health SaaS and EHR vendors (Kipu Health, Alleva, Procentive, BestNotes) whose ideal customer is an addiction treatment facility and who need a clean directory for SDR prospecting; addiction treatment staffing agencies and healthcare recruiters placing addiction counselors, LCSWs, and substance abuse social workers in treatment centers; insurance credentialing firms helping treatment facilities join Medicaid and commercial insurance networks; recovery housing and sober living operators who partner with nearby treatment facilities for referral networks.

data_wanted: SAMHSA N-SSATS (National Survey of Substance Abuse Treatment Services) Public Use Data File — published annually by SAMHSA at https://www.samhsa.gov/data/data-we-collect/n-ssats-national-survey-substance-abuse-treatment-services. Most recent full year: 2022 N-SSATS PUF (2023 data expected later in 2025). Also: SAMHSA's National Directory of Mental Health Treatment Facilities at https://www.samhsa.gov/data/report/national-directory-of-mental-health-treatment-facilities. Key fields per facility: facility name, street address, city, state, ZIP, FIPS county code, facility type (hospital inpatient, residential short-term, residential long-term, outpatient, opioid treatment program/OTP, intensive outpatient, partial hospitalization), ownership type (private for-profit, private non-profit, state government, local/county government, tribal), services offered (medication-assisted treatment, residential detox, medically-managed detox, dual diagnosis, adolescent services, veterans-specific, LGBTQ+-specific, criminal justice-involved), payment types accepted (Medicaid, Medicare, state-funded, private insurance, self-pay/sliding scale), licensed/certified beds, total capacity. Supplemented by the SAMHSA Behavioral Health Treatment Services Locator API at https://findtreatment.gov/locator-api/ for cross-validation. Target: ~15,000 unique facility records.

evidence.quote: N-SSATS Public Use Data File: The National Survey of Substance Abuse Treatment Services collects data from all known substance abuse treatment facilities in the United States. Public use data files are available for download in SAS and SPSS format.

evidence.source: Indivior (Suboxone/buprenorphine manufacturer) — pharmaceutical company that markets to addiction treatment facilities and OTPs confirms the commercial value of a comprehensive treatment facility list for sales territory planning
evidence.quote: Indivior provides buprenorphine-based medication-assisted treatment (MAT) solutions to opioid treatment programs (OTPs), outpatient clinics, and office-based opioid treatment (OBOT) providers across the United States.

evidence.source: Behavioral Health Business (BHB) — trade publication for the addiction treatment industry; notes 15,000+ facilities in the US with $42B+ in annual revenue, confirming a large commercial target market for SaaS and services vendors
evidence.quote: The US behavioral health and addiction treatment industry includes 15,000+ licensed facilities generating approximately $42 billion in annual revenue. Facility operators are active buyers of EHR, revenue cycle management, and staffing services.

willingness_to_pay.signal: Pharmaceutical reps are the highest-conviction buyer: companies like Indivior and BraeBurn fund dedicated sales forces to call on addiction treatment facilities; a $49 CSV of every OTP, inpatient detox, and MAT clinic in a sales territory is worth zero hesitation — a single new formulary win from this list pays back 1,000× in prescription revenue. Behavioral health SaaS SDRs are the second tier: Kipu Health, Alleva, and similar EHR vendors spend heavily on outbound to addiction treatment facilities; a $49 clean facility list is trivially worth one qualified demo call ($5K–$50K ACV per deal). CenterSite charges $500/month for behavioral health directory advertising, proving treatment center operators are accustomed to B2B marketing spend in this vertical. The N-SSATS data is published but almost never surface as a clean flat-file product — it arrives as a SAS export requiring specialized software to open, creating a clear packaging arbitrage.

first_sale_path.angle: Title: 'SAMHSA Substance Abuse Treatment Facility Directory 2024 — 15,000+ US Programs by Type, Services & Payment (CSV)'. Key selling points: (1) Every SAMHSA-registered substance abuse treatment facility in the US — facility name, address, type (OTP/inpatient/outpatient/residential), services offered (MAT/detox/dual-diagnosis), payment accepted (Medicaid/Medicare/private insurance), (2) Direct from SAMHSA N-SSATS public use data — the same government dataset that powers findtreatment.gov, (3) Filter by state, facility type, or service line — find every methadone clinic in Ohio or every adolescent residential program in California, (4) One-time $49 instant CSV — not $500/month. Pharma rep angle: 'Map every OTP and MAT clinic in your territory. 15,000 facilities. $49 once. One spreadsheet.' SaaS SDR angle: 'Your entire addressable market in one CSV — every addiction treatment facility that could use your EHR. Filter by state and program type.'
